retro:
# Retrospective

## What worked

Fresh Opus 5.5 High and Sol Xhigh sessions investigated independently. Prelaunch security triage was completed before code execution. Full reports and targeted follow-ups were retained separately. Conflicting baseline results triggered investigation of the configuration model rather than majority voting. Native package rules plus parsed-pattern controls established a narrow useful result without a desktop slot. No browser was opened and no upstream comment was posted.

## Friction and corrections

The first Sol substitute rule did not model the native package alias chain, and changing only 48 still did not suffice. Its apparent new explicit-default regression was withdrawn, not silently rewritten. Use the real package rules when readily available, and validate baseline behavior before inferring causality.

Opus's initial fixture had many parent-only guards and missing per-producer postconditions; Sol initially asserted the generated file only after invocation. Both acknowledged the omissions. Opus's /tmp/w was namespace-private but outside the requested retained assignment root. A fresh Sol v4 fixture confines its writes to retained output and asserts final generator paths before launch. All original raw evidence remains. The round is not labelled safety-process compliant. No policy waiver or seal was substituted for inspecting child results.

Hyphenated fontconfig names need parsed-name controls. Opus's first ui-monospace rows actually queried ui, so those rows and invalid traces are excluded. Version output on stderr caused Sol's first precondition failure, also preserved and excluded.

Coordinator's brief lifecycle pane read incidentally included a conclusion snippet after one reviewer finished. It was not used in place of reports or exposed to the peer. Future lifecycle checks should use get/file presence first, with pane reads only for a concrete blocker.

## Carry forward

Before executing any generator, enumerate every actual/transitive write target, assert it under retained private output, check each producer and resulting content, and retain stderr from process start. Start from the smallest native configuration chain that reproduces the baseline, not an invented approximation. Stop once material pattern questions are settled; unavailable real UI rendering does not justify expanding substitute experiments.

No confirmed Omadev/tool defect or new infrastructure feature request. All experiments completed synchronously, with no owned persistent handles requiring cleanup. No Claude quota signal.
comment:
One fontconfig-level regression remains: `ui-monospace` loses the selected family.

**Verified:** After selecting `Sarasa Mono SC`, generic `monospace` still puts that family first, while an explicit `DejaVu Sans Mono` request now keeps its own family first.

## Preserve the selected font for `ui-monospace`

The new first-family test in `bin/omarchy-font-set` misses `ui-monospace`, which `50-omarchy.conf` explicitly aliases to `monospace`. Its first family remains `ui-monospace`, not `JetBrainsMono Nerd Font`.

Real fontconfig 2.18.3 pattern substitution, with a modeled package configuration order and freshly generated user rules:

| Request | Before | PR |
|---|---|---|
| `monospace` | Selected family first | Selected family first |
| `DejaVu Sans Mono` | Selected family first | Requested family first |
| `ui-monospace` | Selected family first | Selected family absent; list starts `ui-monospace, JetBrainsMono Nerd Font` |

**Impact:** The configured `ui-monospace` alias no longer carries the user's selected monospace family through fontconfig substitution. Actual browser rendering was not tested.

**Suggested change:** Handle first-family `ui-monospace` explicitly alongside the new packaged-default match. A diagnostic second match restored the selected family in this substitution path without changing the sampled `monospace`, DejaVu or explicit-default results.

**Documentation correction:** The new comment's “only remaps true generic monospace patterns” is too broad. Explicit `JetBrainsMono Nerd Font` requests are still remapped, a pre-existing limitation already noted in #12779. State that exception in the comment and PR description.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head `8c86bc46`; real base/head setters and fontconfig pattern substitution, with synthetic font inventory and stubbed desktop side effects. Configuration order was modeled, not taken from a live installation. No installed-font matching, browser or GUI rendering checks. Existing generated rules require rerunning `omarchy font set` to pick up this change.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium coordination, independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, followed by evidence reconciliation and an Astra Medium editorial check.
